result.title: Learning from the Right Regions: Class-Conditioned Explanation Guidance for Medical Imaging
result.comment: Submitted to the Explainable and Trustworthy AI for Clinical Decision Support Systems Workshop, IEEE BIBM 2026
result.summary: Deep neural networks can achieve strong predictive performance in medical imaging while relying on regions unrelated to the predicted finding. Explanation-guided learning can address this problem, but multi-label classification introduces a key challenge: multiple abnormalities may coexist in an image, requiring each prediction to align with its corresponding spatial evidence. We propose a class-conditioned explanation-guided learning framework that constructs a separate explanation for each positive class and penalizes evidence outside its class-specific annotated regions. We instantiate the framework using Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM) and evaluate it on 14 abnormalities using EfficientNet-B1, ViT-B/16, ViT-B/32, and Swin-B. Explanation guidance substantially improves annotation alignment across all architectures: All-Saliency Precision increases from 0.140 to 0.625, 0.052 to 0.551, 0.060 to 0.403, and 0.095 to 0.570, respectively. These improvements are accompanied by smaller, architecture-dependent changes in classification performance. Our results show that class-conditioned explanation guidance can substantially improve where multi-label classifiers concentrate their explanatory evidence while largely preserving predictive performance.

AI.brief_summary: 提出类条件解释引导学习框架：为每个阳性类别单独构造 Grad-CAM 解释，惩罚落在该类标注区域之外的证据，从而在多标签医学影像上提升证据与标注区域的对齐，且分类性能变化不大。
